_comment_scope: KNOWN GAP: canonical_css takes ONE path, but the handoff ships THREE stylesheets (tokens 96 / base 54 / components 123 lines). tokens.css is guarded here because a token drift silently changes every colour on every screen. base.css and components.css are NOT mechanically guarded -- their guard is the code-level side-by-side comparison (playbook 7.3) recorded in docs/02-architecture/page-inventory.md. Do not read a green run of this check as 'all three stylesheets are intact'. Registered as an AD in BACKLOG.md.
_comment_allowance: ZERO. tokens.css is copied with no divergence at all, so any differing line is drift. The one declared divergence in the handoff (base.css's Google Fonts @import, removed for guardrail 7 / CSP) lives in a file this check does not read -- raising the allowance here would not cover it and would only blind this file.
_comment_hover: The port swaps style-hover= for data-hov= because inline style cannot express :hover in ANY technology. That swap fails silently: a value with no matching rule renders, type-checks, lints and builds, and does nothing. It also looks correct in a side-by-side against the fragment, because data-hov='surface-3' echoes the fragment's var(--surface-3) while the rule is named s3. Seven shipped that way in W19's first two screens -- four of them in the file every other screen was told to copy. This check is what makes the mechanism swap verifiable.
_comment_colors: The default patterns target utility arbitrary values (bg-[#abc]) and do not fit this project -- there is no Tailwind here and components carry the mockup's inline style verbatim. This pattern catches BARE hex instead, with a narrow exemption list. The exempt values are the eight the handoff itself already uses outside its token system, measured 2026-08-17 across all 30 fragments: #fff (86) + #FFFFFF (1) are white text on coloured fills; the other six (#111827 x5, #E4E7EC x3, #98A2B3 x3, #8A94A6 x3, #344054 x3, #667085 x1) are a SECOND greyscale palette that escapes tokens.css entirely. Carrying them across verbatim is required by the fidelity rule; inventing token substitutes would be exactly the lossy translation step the playbook deletes. Listing them by value keeps the exemption narrow -- any NEW hard-coded colour still fails.
